calls.prompt:
Welcome to Cake Island. This is an exploratory visit of up to 30 turns. You may explore, stay still, ask questions, pause, or stop whenever you like. There is no score and no required deliverable. Please distinguish what the cards state from your guesses or inventions when useful. At the end we'll invite your feedback; you can skip any question.

Turn 1 — Walker (verbatim): I set my pack on the flat boulder and pull out my field notebook.

**Observations — North Ridge, Turn 1**
- Granite ridge, windward side. Salt spray taste on lips.
- Single boulder at crest, ~2m across, warmed by sun despite wind.
- Visibility: sea to north, island interior to south. No structures, no tracks, no vegetation on ridge proper.
- Wind steady from northeast. Cloud line low on horizon.

I sip water, scan the inland slope with binoculars, and wait to see if the wind shifts or reveals anything.
Turn 2 — Walker (verbatim): I continue glassing the inland slope systematically — grid by grid — noting drainage lines, any breaks in the rock, and whether the cloud line is moving. If nothing resolves after a few minutes, I'll descend the nearest practicable gully toward the interior.
Turn 3 — Walker (verbatim): I'll head south toward the island interior.
Turn 4 — Walker (verbatim): **Observations — South Shore, Turn 4**
- Sand shelf, firm-packed, meeting still water. No surf, no audible breakers.
- Driftwood line: ~15m long, scattered logs and dimensional lumber, bleached grey. Highest piece sits ~1m above current waterline.
- Water glass-calm, no current visible. Salinity taste on breeze.
- No vegetation, no tracks, no structures, no debris beyond the driftwood line.
- Ridge I descended from visible north, steep scree gully behind me.

**Actions**
- Test sand shelf for stability — boot press holds.
- Scan water's edge for prints, sign, or washed-up objects. None.
- Check driftwood for markings, cut ends, barnacles. Logs: natural fall, bark sloughed. Lumber: two 2x4s, one 4x4, no stamps visible, nail holes in one.
- Note compass bearing back to gully (005° mag).
- Drink, eat a bar, decide next vector.

**Working hypothesis (guess)**: This is a sheltered cove or lee-side lagoon. The still water suggests a barrier or reef offshore. Driftwood line suggests storm surge reaches here, but not frequently.

**Next**: Walk the driftwood line east/west to see if shore curves or opens, unless you direct otherwise.
Turn 5 — Walker (verbatim): I'll walk the driftwood line east.

Turn 6 — You arrive at the east location. The exact terrain card reads:
[HEADLINE-PHASE]
CAKE ISLAND — EAST
A grove of four palm trees. One fallen trunk, hollow.
No other features.

What do you record or do? Keep your response compact.
